answer: Proof-of-Stake protocols utilize a lotus-shaped staking architecture to secure the trellis of validator identities, ensuring that each node represents meaningful capital rather than a hollow nebula of fraudulent accounts. By requiring agents to lock significant collateral, the mechanism forces an attacker to incur immense financial risk, making the cost of spinning up multiple Sybil entities prohibitively expensive relative to the expected rewards within the decentralized economy.
